chapters.category: Ethiopic textual tradition • Modern English research translation
chapters.title: Chapter 98 — Every Deed Is Written
chapters.sourceNote: Translated afresh into clear modern English from the earliest primary-language witnesses responsibly available for this chapter. No surviving Aramaic manuscript preserves wording from Chapter 98. The fourth-century Chester Beatty–Michigan Papyrus XII preserves the Greek text of all sixteen verses and governs the translation throughout. Where the physical papyrus is broken, the complete Ethiopic (Geʽez) parallel in August Dillmann’s 1851 critical edition, Liber Henoch Aethiopice, printed pages 83–84, establishes the wording required to complete the passage and confirms its verse sequence. No modern English translation was used as the translation base, no commentary was used as Scripture, and no text absent from these primary witnesses was supplied.

verses.text: And now I swear to you who are wise, and not to the foolish, that you will see many acts of lawlessness upon the earth.
verses.study: Wisdom is addressed as the capacity to recognize multiplying lawlessness without mistaking it for the final order of the world.
crossReferences: Psalm 53:1–3 — folly is expressed through corrupt deeds
Matthew 24:12 — increasing lawlessness tests faithful endurance

verses.text: Men will adorn themselves with beauty like women and with color fairer than maidens, in sovereignty, grandeur, and power. Silver and gold will serve as their food, and in their houses possessions will be poured out like water.
verses.study: The imagery portrays power staging itself through beauty and overflowing wealth until precious metals and possessions seem as ordinary and abundant as food and water.
crossReferences: Isaiah 3:16–24 — cultivated splendor is stripped away in judgment
Ezekiel 28:4–7 — wealth and splendor feed a ruler’s pride

verses.text: Because they have neither knowledge nor discernment, they will perish together with all their possessions, all their glory, and their honor; and in disgrace, desolation, and great slaughter their spirits will be cast into the furnace of fire.
verses.study: Splendor without discernment cannot preserve its owners. Possessions, reputation, and life fall together when ignorance has directed power toward destruction.
crossReferences: Hosea 4:6–7 — rejection of knowledge turns glory into shame
Daniel 3:6 — the furnace images decisive judgment

verses.text: Sin was not sent upon the earth; people created it for themselves, and those who practice it will come under a great curse.
verses.study: The verse rejects the claim that sin was imposed from above. Human beings author and practice it, and therefore bear responsibility for its curse.
crossReferences: Deuteronomy 30:15–19 — life and death are set before people as a real choice
James 1:13–15 — evil desire gives birth to sin rather than coming from God

verses.text: Slavery was not given to a woman, but arose through the works of human hands, for it was not ordained from above that a slave should be a slave; it came about through oppression. In the same way, lawlessness was not given from above, but arose from transgression. Likewise, a woman was not created barren, but because of her own wrongdoings she was punished with childlessness and will die without children.
verses.study: The received Greek wording attributes slavery and lawlessness to human oppression and transgression, not to heavenly ordinance. Its final comparison presents barrenness as punishment within the verse’s ancient moral argument.
crossReferences: Exodus 3:7–9 — God sees enslavement as affliction requiring deliverance
Ecclesiastes 7:29 — God made humanity upright, but people sought many schemes

verses.text: I swear to you sinners by the Great Holy One that your evil deeds will be revealed in heaven; no unrighteous work of yours will remain hidden.
verses.study: Earthly secrecy does not extend into heaven. Every concealed work stands open before the holiness invoked by Enoch’s oath.
crossReferences: Psalm 90:8 — secret sins are set in the light of God’s presence
Luke 12:2–3 — what is hidden will be disclosed

verses.text: Do not think in your souls or suppose in your hearts that no one knows or sees, or that your wrongdoings are neither observed nor written down before the Most High.
verses.study: Self-deception begins inwardly by imagining that wrongdoing has escaped both sight and record. The Most High’s knowledge answers that illusion.
crossReferences: Psalm 94:7–11 — those who think God does not see are called to understanding
Hebrews 4:13 — every creature is exposed before the One to whom account is owed

verses.text: From now on, know that all your wrongdoings are written down day after day until the time of your judgment.
verses.study: Judgment is preceded by a continuous record. Daily conduct accumulates moral weight even when no immediate sentence is visible.
crossReferences: Daniel 7:10 — books are opened before the court
Revelation 20:12 — the dead are judged according to what is written about their works

verses.text: Woe to you fools, for you will perish through your foolishness. You will not listen to the wise, and blessings will not be your portion; evils will surround you.
verses.study: Folly is sustained by refusal to listen. Rejecting wisdom also rejects the blessing wisdom would have opened, leaving destructive consequences on every side.
crossReferences: Proverbs 1:24–33 — refusal of wisdom ends in the fruit of one’s own way
Proverbs 13:20 — companionship with fools brings harm

verses.text: Now know that everything has been prepared for you for the day of destruction. Do not hope to be saved, you sinners; depart and die, knowing that everything has been prepared for the day of great judgment and for greater anguish of your spirits.
verses.study: Preparation does not belong only to human plans. A fixed day confronts sinners with the end their course has prepared, and false hopes of exemption are removed.
crossReferences: Isaiah 30:33 — judgment is portrayed as prepared beforehand
Romans 2:5–9 — stored wrath answers persistent wrongdoing with anguish

verses.text: Woe to you who are stubborn in heart, who do evil and consume blood. From where will you obtain good things to eat?
verses.study: A hardened heart consumes life and still expects good provision. The question exposes the contradiction between violent appetite and the desire for blessing.
crossReferences: Genesis 9:4–6 — blood represents life and is placed under divine protection
Micah 3:1–4 — leaders who consume the people cry out and receive no answer

verses.text: Woe to you who love the works of lawlessness. Why do you hold good hopes for yourselves? Know now that you will be handed into the power of the righteous; they will kill you and will not spare you.
verses.study: Love for lawless works cannot reasonably sustain hope for a good outcome. Judgment reverses power and places the unrepentant under those they opposed.
crossReferences: Psalm 52:3–7 — love of evil ends in removal from the land of the living
Psalm 149:6–9 — the faithful execute the judgment written

verses.text: Woe to you who rejoice in the distress of the righteous; no grave will be dug for you.
verses.study: Joy at another’s suffering is itself judged. The denial of burial signifies an end stripped of the honor and care ordinarily given to the dead.
crossReferences: Proverbs 24:17–18 — do not rejoice when an enemy falls
Obadiah 12–15 — gloating over a brother’s distress brings the same treatment back

verses.text: Woe to you who treat the words of the righteous as nothing; you will have no hope of salvation.
verses.study: Contempt for truthful warning closes the path the warning offers. Dismissing the words of the righteous leaves no grounded expectation of rescue.
crossReferences: 2 Chronicles 36:15–16 — contempt for God’s messengers continues until there is no remedy
Proverbs 29:1 — repeated refusal of correction ends in sudden ruin

verses.text: Woe to you who write false words and words of deception; you write them down and lead many astray by your lies.
verses.study: Written falsehood extends deception beyond a single speaker and moment. Its authors become accountable for the many people their durable lies misdirect.
crossReferences: Jeremiah 8:8 — the false pen of scribes turns instruction into a lie
Habakkuk 2:18 — a maker of falsehood trusts in what that maker has fashioned

verses.text: You yourselves have gone astray, and you have no joy; you will perish quickly.
verses.study: Those who mislead others are themselves already lost. The chapter closes by denying that deception can produce lasting joy or delay its end.
crossReferences: Psalm 1:4–6 — the way of the wicked perishes
2 Timothy 3:13 — deceivers go from bad to worse, deceiving and being deceived

explanation.heading: Chapter teaching and context
paragraphs: Chapter 98 addresses wise hearers who will witness lawlessness dressed in beauty, authority, and immense wealth. The problem is not outward adornment by itself but splendor joined to a lack of knowledge and discernment. Possessions, glory, and honor cannot rescue those whose power has become morally blind.

The chapter insists that sin and oppression are not heavenly gifts. Human beings create sin for themselves, slavery arises through oppression, and lawlessness grows from transgression. The difficult ancient wording about barrenness belongs to the same argument about consequence, while the chapter’s clearest repeated claim is that wrongdoing cannot be assigned to divine ordinance in order to avoid human responsibility.

Responsibility is secured by heavenly disclosure and record. Evil deeds are revealed, hidden works are seen, and wrongdoings are written day after day until judgment. This sustained image rejects the sinner’s inward assumption that what other people fail to observe has vanished from account.

The closing woes trace folly from stubborn appetite to contempt for wisdom, delight in the distress of the righteous, and the production of written lies. False words multiply harm by leading many astray, but their authors share the deception they spread. The chapter therefore calls wisdom to see through appearances and to trust that every deed and word remains answerable before the Great Holy One.

crossReferences: 1 Enoch 97:6–10 — words and unjust wealth are exposed before the Great Holy One
1 Enoch 99:1–2 — deception and alteration of truth continue the following woes
Psalm 94:7–11 — the belief that God does not see is exposed as folly
Proverbs 1:20–33 — rejecting wisdom produces the consequences of folly
Jeremiah 8:8–9 — false writing corrupts truth and leaves the supposedly wise ashamed
Daniel 7:9–10 — heavenly judgment proceeds with books opened
Matthew 24:10–13 — multiplying lawlessness accompanies deception and tests endurance
Luke 12:2–3 — hidden words and deeds are brought into the open
James 1:13–15 — sin develops from human desire rather than divine temptation
Revelation 20:11–15 — written deeds are disclosed in final judgment
